topic: What beam management strategies are needed to mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band?
consensus_response: High-gain beams in the 57-66 GHz band reduce angular spread but increase sensitivity to user distribution variability. To mitigate this, adaptive beamforming and power allocation strategies are essential due to high gain beams' sensitivity to user distribution variability. Artificial intelligence (AI) can optimize these strategies by predicting user movements and weather conditions for proactive adjustments that maintain optimal performance while reducing budget costs associated with frequent reconfigurations. Analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) handle the high data rates required for mmWave frequencies, enabling real-time signal processing and beamforming adjustments to minimize interference and maximize spectral efficiency.
reference_context: The 57-66 GHz band requires high-gain beams due to severe path loss, limiting angular spreads. System parameters such as beamforming granularity and channel selectivity properties must be reconsidered for above 6 GHz bands due to changes in mmWave propagation characteristics.
